display_name: Trigger the scheduled self-vet (daily L1 heartbeat)
description: Fire the daily L1-only self-vet of the platform's own worktree on a single-slot background executor, and return IMMEDIATELY with a receipt: {self_vet: 'started'} if the run was submitted, or {self_vet: 'already_running'} if a run is already in flight (the single slot IS the lease — a fire while busy is a no-op, no new lease machinery). This is an EDGE_SINK cron heartbeat: it does NO scanning inline (a full L1 self-vet is minutes; running it on the dispatch thread would stall the action queue), so the scan runs on a daemon thread off the dispatch path. The background run goes through the persisting L1 path (one vetting_runs row per run — this accumulates the run-over-run trend baseline) and, ONLY when its blocker or high finding counts worsen versus the previous run, queues a regression note to memory (tag code_vetting:self_vet_regression) for the operator to see later; a clean or improved run is silent. It runs no AI critics or inference. Registered for a daily cron; also invokable on demand to kick off a self-vet now. It does not accept a target — the self-vet is always the platform's own worktree.
embedding_description: Kick off the scheduled background self-vet of the codebase and return immediately: start the recurring lightweight self-scan that records one trend row per run and pings only on regression, or report that a self-vet is already in flight. The background heartbeat scan, scheduled rather than interactive.
